---
title: Deploy to Vercel
description: Deploy a Pluto site to a host with a server runtime.
navigation:
  icon: i-simple-icons-vercel
---

A Pluto site needs a server runtime. The admin routes and the public read routes run on the server. A static export does not work for the GitHub CMS.

The templates name Vercel, Netlify, and Node as hosts with a server runtime. This guide uses Vercel as the example.

## Step 1: push the project

Push the project to a GitHub repository. For the GitHub CMS, this repository also holds the content.

## Step 2: import the project

Import the repository in Vercel. Vercel detects Nuxt.

## Step 3: set the environment variables

Set the variables in the settings of the Vercel project.

### GitHub CMS

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `PLUTO_CMS_REPO` | `owner/name` of the repository |
| `PLUTO_CMS_APP_SLUG` | The URL name of the GitHub App |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_SESSION_PASSWORD` | 32 characters or more |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_APP_ID` | The App ID |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | The Client ID |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | The client secret |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY` | The private key on one line, with `\n` for line breaks |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_ALLOWED_USERS` | Optional. Comma-separated GitHub logins. Only these users can sign in, even with push access. |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_READ_TOKEN` | Optional. A read-only token. It replaces the installation token for anonymous reads. |

The session password, the GitHub App values, and the optional values are run-time variables. The module does not check them at build time.

The template uses the `github` storage in production. See [GitHub CMS setup](/github-cms/setup).

Add the production callback URL to the GitHub App: `https://<your-site>/api/_pluto/auth/github/callback`.

### Supabase

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | The Supabase project URL |
| `SUPABASE_KEY` | The publishable key |
| `DATABASE_URL` | The Postgres connection string. The admin uses it to apply migrations. When it is not set, the setup and migrations pages ask for the string. |

These variables are optional. Set them in the environment of the **running server**, not in the build environment:

| Variable | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `NUXT_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | Invites through the invite API of Supabase |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_RESEND_API_KEY` | Pluto mail with Resend |
| `NUXT_PLUTO_MAIL_FROM` | The From address |

::warning
The mail variables are run-time values. Do not put them in the build environment.
::

## Step 4: deploy

Deploy the project. Open `/admin` and sign in.

For a Supabase site, the first visit goes to `/admin/setup`. See [Supabase layer](/supabase).

## Commits and rebuilds

A content save in the GitHub CMS is a commit. On Vercel, Pluto finds the repository from the Vercel variables, so you need not set `plutoCms.github.repo`. By default, the commit message ends with `[skip ci]`, so a host that honors the marker does not rebuild on each save.

- A site that reads its content at run time, such as the blog template, needs no rebuild for a content change.
- A site that builds its pages from the content files must rebuild on each save. Set `plutoCms.commit.skipDeploy` to `false`.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  plutoCms: {
    commit: { skipDeploy: false }
  }
})
```

::note
Not every host honors `[skip ci]`. Test it on your project, and check the documentation of your host. Vercel has an "Ignored Build Step" setting that lets a project skip a build by rule.
::
